Overview -

Company Information -

Contoso, Ltd is a multinational retail company that builds, deploys, and manages generative AI and agent-based solutions by using Microsoft

Foundry.

Existing Environment -

Identity Environment -

Contoso uses Microsoft Entra ID for identity management, authentication, and authorization capabilities that enable agents to access

organizational resources and services.

Contoso recently formed a new AI engineering team named Agent1Dev Team to optimize and maintain existing AI solutions.

The team collaborates with solution architects, DevOps engineers, and security engineers to design, implement. monitor, and secure AI

applications.

Contoso also has a team named Agent1Test Team that is responsible for validating AI solutions before the solution deployments.

Generative Environment -

Contoso has a Microsoft Foundry deployment that contains two projects named Project1 and Project2.

Project1 -

Project1 contains a customer support agent named Agent1 that assists customers with product inquiries and troubleshooting requests.

Agent1 has the following configurations:

Agent1 uses a base model deployment.

A safety evaluation pipeline is NOT enabled.

Tool invocation approval workflows are NOT enabled.

Conversation memory constraints are NOT configured.

Agent1 interacts with customers by using digital support channels and answers general questions about Contoso products.

Project1 is deployed to an Azure region located in the European Union (EU).

Agent1Dev Team will use Project1 to optimize and maintain Agent1.

Project2 -

Project2 contains a deployed video generation model. The marketing department at Contoso has access to Project2 and plans to use the model to

develop a video creation solution.

Development of the solution is incomplete.

Data Environment -

Contoso stores product-related information in Azure resources that support AI applications.

The Azure environment contains an Azure Blob Storage account named storage1 that stores product detail sheets for all the Contoso products.

The product sheets include specifications, feature descriptions, and product support information that Agent1 can use to answer customer

questions. The product sheets are stored in the PDF format.

Problem Statements -

Contoso identifies the following issues:

Agent1 has only general knowledge of the Contoso products.

A recent chat interaction with Agent1 was analyzed for sentiment. The results of the analysis have NOT been processed yet.

Agent1 does NOT use the detailed product information in the product sheets stored in storage1 when responding to customer questions.

The finance department at Contoso reports that vendor invoices must be reviewed manually to ensure that the invoices match the terms defined in

the vendor contracts. The invoices contain tables, logos, and varied layouts that make the documents difficult to process consistently.

Requirements -

Planned Changes -

Contoso plans to implement the following changes:

Implement a solution for Project1 that analyzes the vendor invoices by evaluating both the visual layout and the textual content of the invoices, so

that the invoice details can be verified against the vendor contract terms.

Update the base model deployment used by Agent1 and standardize the model version to ensure continuity and consistent responses.

Enable Agent1 to retrieve and use the detailed product information from the product sheets stored in storage1.

Implement an indexing solution for the product sheets that Agent1 can use to answer customer questions.

Complete the development of the video creation solution.

Technical Requirements -

Contoso identifies the following technical requirements:

The model deployment used by Agent1 must support scalable, high-throughput generative AI workloads and dynamically scale to handle variable

customer support traffic, without requiring reserved throughput capacity.

The product sheets must be processed by using an indexing pipeline that enables semantic and vector search, so that Agent1 can retrieve the

relevant product information.

Responses generated by using the product sheet information must be relevant, complete, and accurate.

Agent1 must be able to use the product sheets to answer natural language questions about product details.

The model version used by Agent1 must remain consistent to ensure stable responses.

The data processed by the model must remain within the EU.

Security and Compliance Requirements

Contoso identifies the following security and compliance requirements:

API keys must NOT be used to access Foundry-deployed models.

Access to the Azure resources must follow the principle of least privilege.

The developers at Contoso must authenticate to Microsoft Foundry resources by using Microsoft Entra authentication.

Access to Project1 must be assigned to the members of Agent1Dev Team by using a security group named SC_Agent1_Dev.

Access to Project1 must be assigned to the members of Agent1Test Team by using a security group named SC_Agent1_Test.

Agent1 must never reveal customer information, even if a document that contains customer data is added erroneously to the product sheet

repository in storage1.

The product sheets might contain images that include embedded text. Agent1 must be protected from malicious instructions potentially hidden

within the images.

Business Requirements -

Contoso identifies the following business requirements:

Users that interact with Agent1 must have a personalized experience in future interactions, including the ability for Agent1 to retain conversation

context and recall relevant information from previous interactions.

Agent1 must answer questions only about the products sold by Contoso.

Global Standard can route inference traffic across supported global regions. That conflicts with the requirement that model processing remain within the EU.
Global Provisioned uses reserved provisioned throughput and can route processing globally. The scenario explicitly requires dynamic scaling without reserved throughput and requires EU data residency.
Upgrading when the current version expires still allows the deployed model version to change automatically later, so it does not guarantee a consistent version.

options.text: Opt out of automatic model version upgrades
options.explanation: Regional Standard provides consumption-based dynamic scaling without reserved PTUs and keeps processing tied to the selected region. Opting out of automatic upgrades keeps the deployed model version stable until the team changes it deliberately.

options.text: Upgrade once a new default version becomes available
options.explanation: This policy upgrades the deployment whenever a new default version becomes available. That can change model behavior and therefore conflicts with the requirement for a consistent model version.

communityNotes.summary: The discussion distinguishes regional Standard from Global Standard and provisioned deployments. Standard is the defensible choice because the workload must scale without reserved throughput while processing remains in the selected EU region.
caveats: Global Standard offers highly elastic throughput, but it can route inference outside the selected region.
Data Zone Standard could be relevant in a different option set, but it is not offered in this question.

question:
You are planning a Microsoft Foundry project named Project1 that will contain multiple agents. Each agent will access the same Azure AI Search

resource.

You need to recommend a solution to centrally manage the Azure AI Search credentials within Project1. The solution must be implemented across

all the agents.

What should you recommend?

options.text: Enable role-based access control (RBAC) for the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: Azure RBAC controls which identities may access the Search resource and what operations they may perform. It manages authorization, not a reusable project-level connection and its credentials.

options.text: Disable key-based access control on the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: Disabling key-based access forces clients to use Microsoft Entra authentication. This improves credential security but does not centrally register the Search connection for all project agents.

options.text: Add a connection to the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: A project connection stores the endpoint and authentication configuration once and allows every agent in the project to reuse it. RBAC and private endpoints solve authorization and networking concerns rather than central connection management.

options.text: Create a managed private endpoint that connects to the Azure AI Search resource.
options.explanation: A managed private endpoint keeps traffic to Azure AI Search on a private network path. It solves network isolation, not central credential and connection management.

You need to ensure that App1 meets the following requirements:

Authenticates by using a Microsoft Entra managed identity

Sends prompts to a deployed model by using the Azure OpenAI Responses API

How should you complete the Python code? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: AzureKeyCredential authenticates with a static service key. It cannot satisfy the requirement to use a Microsoft Entra managed identity.
ClientSecretCredential uses a tenant ID, client ID, and stored client secret. It is an application credential, not managed identity authentication.
DefaultAzureCredential can obtain a managed-identity token without storing a key or client secret. responses.create is the Responses API operation that sends a new prompt.
compact reduces stored conversation context so it consumes fewer tokens. It does not send the prompt and create the requested model response.
DefaultAzureCredential can obtain a managed-identity token without storing a key or client secret. responses.create is the Responses API operation that sends a new prompt.
retrieve fetches a response that was created previously. It cannot create a new response from the current prompt.

answerTemplate.content:
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient

credential = {{credential}}()

    endpoint="https://contosoai.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/project1",
    credential=credential,
)
with project_client.get_openai_client() as openai_client:
    response = openai_client.responses.{{responsesMethod}}(
        model="trail-guide-chat",
        input="Create a 3-day hiking itinerary near Seattle.",
    )

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains a workflow for a customer support triage process.

You have an Ask a question node that stores user responses in a local variable named Var01.

You need to create the following Power Fx expressions:

An if/else condition expression that ensures that Var01 contains a value

A Send message expression that returns the stored user response in uppercase

How should you configure the expressions? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: IsBlank(Local.Var01) is true when the local variable has no value. The workflow needs the opposite condition so it continues after the user supplied an answer.
IsEmpty is intended for an empty table or collection in Power Fx. Var01 stores one response value, so IsBlank is the appropriate test.
Not(IsBlank(Local.Var01)) is true only after the local response variable contains a value, allowing the next step to run.
{Local.Var01} inserts the response exactly as entered. It does not apply the required uppercase transformation.
{Upper(Local.Var01)} reads the correctly scoped local variable and converts its text to uppercase.
{Upper(Var01)} performs uppercase conversion but omits the Local scope, so it does not reference the stored local workflow variable correctly.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains a customer support agent built by using the Foundry Agent Service.

The agent uploads user-provided screenshots to Azure Storage through a ticketing tool and receives a blob URL for additional reasoning.

You need to use image moderation during agent runs and prevent harmful content from being returned during runs. Azure AI Content Safety must

access the images by using the blob URL. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

What should you configure for Content Safety? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Select Tool call and set Action to Block.
options.explanation: Blocking Tool call output would stop content returned by a tool. The risky data enters as user input and can appear in the model output, so this targets the wrong stages.

options.text: Select User input and Output and set Action to Annotate.
options.explanation: Annotate labels detections in user input and output but allows the content to continue. It does not enforce the required blocking action.

options.text: Select User input and Tool response and set Action to Annotate.
options.explanation: This annotates user input and tool responses without blocking them, and it monitors tool response rather than the model output required by the scenario.

options.text: Select User input, Output, Tool response, and Tool call and set Action to Block.
options.explanation: This applies blocking across user input, model output, tool responses, and tool calls, preventing detected unsafe or disallowed content from continuing at any stage.
Storage access keys are long-lived shared secrets. They violate the requirement for identity-based, keyless access.

options.text: A user-assigned identity that is assigned the Storage Queue Data Contributor role
options.explanation: This identity has Queue Data Contributor, which authorizes queue data. The tool uploads screenshots as blobs, so it needs a blob data role instead.

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity that is assigned the Storage Blob Data Reader role
options.explanation: A system-assigned managed identity with Storage Blob Data Reader provides keyless, least-privilege access to read the uploaded screenshots without granting write or delete permissions.

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity that is assigned the Storage Blob Data Contributor role
options.explanation: A system-assigned identity is keyless, but it belongs to the resource it is enabled on. The scenario requires the specified user-assigned identity so the same identity and permissions can be managed independently.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent named PaymentAgent.

PaymentAgent includes a function tool that issues customer refunds by using an external API.

You are creating a workflow in YAML.

You need to ensure that the workflow pauses for human approval and continues with the refund step only after approval is granted.

How should you complete the workflow definition? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.explanation: ask_question pauses the workflow and collects a human response, providing the approval checkpoint before the refund tool can run.
basic_chat runs a model conversation step. It does not pause execution and collect an explicit human approval decision.
data_transformation reshapes or maps workflow data. It cannot ask a person to approve the proposed refund.
approval == "approved" checks the human answer explicitly, so the refund tool runs only after approval.
Checking whether the proposal has output only confirms that a refund was proposed. It does not confirm that a human approved it.
A condition of true always executes the refund path and therefore bypasses the approval safeguard.

    agent: PaymentAgent

    agent: PaymentAgent
    condition: {{condition}}

question:
You have an Azure Speech in Foundry Tools resource that hosts a custom speech to text model deployed to a custom endpoint. An agent uses the

endpoint to perform real-time speech recognition.

You are approaching the expiration date of the custom speech to text model.

What is the expected behavior when the model expires?

options.text: Speech recognition requests will return a 4xx error until a new custom model is deployed.
options.explanation: A 4xx failure is the documented behavior for some batch-transcription uses of an expired model. Real-time recognition through the custom endpoint instead falls back to the current base model for the locale.

options.text: Speech recognition requests will continue to use the expired custom model until the model is removed manually.
options.explanation: An expired model is no longer used indefinitely for real-time recognition. The custom endpoint falls back to the latest supported base model for the locale.

options.text: Speech recognition requests will fall back to the most recent base model for the same locale.
options.explanation: For real-time recognition through a custom endpoint, an expired custom model falls back to the latest base model for the same locale. The 4xx behavior applies to batch transcription.

options.text: The custom model will be deleted automatically when the model expires.
options.explanation: Expiration stops the custom model from being used, but it does not automatically delete the model resource. Deletion and expiration are separate lifecycle actions.

communityNotes.summary: A custom endpoint and batch transcription behave differently after model expiration. Real-time recognition through a custom endpoint falls back to the latest base model for the locale; batch transcription against an expired model fails with a 4xx response.

question:
You have a Microsoft Foundry project that contains an agent. The agent has a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool that queries a knowledge base

stored in Azure AI Search.

Some agent runs return answers from the base model without invoking the knowledge base, which results in responses without grounded

citations.

You are provided with the following code snippet that runs the agent.

You need to add the correct tool _choice parameter to the code to deterministically force the agent to invoke the MCP tool on each run.

What should you add?

options.explanation: Setting tool_choice to required prevents the model from skipping tools and answering directly. Auto leaves that decision to the model.
tool_choice set to auto lets the model decide whether to call a tool, so a tool call is not guaranteed. tool_choice set to required forces the model to call a tool during the run.
Selecting a knowledge-base tool type would target that specific tool category if supported. It does not express the rule that at least one tool of any available type must be called.

The agent must receive continuous audio input, convert the input into text for reasoning, and then return spoken responses to a user. The

workflow must meet the following requirements:

Support turn-taking dynamics, where the agent begins to generate the speech output before the user finishes speaking.

Operate with low latency to maintain conversational experience.

You need to enable both speech to text and text to speech in a real-time agent interaction.

options.text: Use batch transcription to convert the audio input and return text responses from the agent.
options.explanation: Batch transcription processes prerecorded audio asynchronously rather than providing live conversational speech recognition. Text to speech synthesizes spoken audio from text; it does not transcribe incoming speech.

options.explanation: A conversational voice agent needs streaming speech recognition for input and text-to-speech synthesis for output; embeddings and translation do not provide that turn-taking loop.

options.explanation: Audio embeddings represent acoustic content numerically for comparison or downstream models. They are not reversible speech-to-text and text-to-speech conversion steps.

options.text: Use speech translation to convert the audio into another language and return the translated text.
options.explanation: Speech translation recognizes spoken audio and translates it into another language. Text to speech synthesizes spoken audio from text; it does not transcribe incoming speech.

options.explanation: Document Translation translates complete files while preserving document structure. Live transcript segments are streaming text, so translating each segment is the appropriate API pattern.

options.text: Split the mixed-language segments into single-language segments and translate each segment separately.
options.explanation: Splitting mixed-language input into single-language segments gives Translator a consistent source language for each request and avoids mistranslating embedded segments.

options.explanation: SSML phoneme elements specify the exact pronunciation of technical terms using a phonetic alphabet, directly correcting pronunciation.

options.text: Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to apply say as rules.
options.explanation: SSML say-as controls how text such as dates, numbers, characters, or telephone numbers is interpreted. It is less precise than phonemes for specialized terminology.

options.text: Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) to adjust the prosody of the voice.
options.explanation: SSML prosody changes pitch, speaking rate, volume, or contour. It changes delivery but not the phonetic pronunciation of a technical term.

options.text: From Azure OpenAI use the Whisper model.
options.explanation: Whisper is a speech-to-text model that transcribes audio. It does not synthesize speech or correct text-to-speech pronunciation.

options.text: Add allowed groups to each index entry
options.explanation: Storing allowed group IDs on each document creates the security metadata needed for document-level filtering.
Creating one index per group physically separates data but duplicates indexes, complicates ingestion, and is unnecessary for document-level security trimming.

options.text: Send access tokens from Microsoft Entra ID, with the search request.
options.explanation: Sending the user's access token authenticates the caller to Search, but Search does not automatically infer document filters from that token in the standard security-trimming pattern.
Retrieving every group in the directory is unnecessary and expensive. The application only needs the current user's group memberships.

options.text: Retrieve the group memberships of the user
options.explanation: Retrieving the current user's group memberships provides the values that can be matched against each document's allowed-groups field.

options.text: Supply the groups as a filter for the search requests
options.explanation: Supplying those group IDs as a Search filter restricts results to documents the user is allowed to access.
